assertions.text: CONTRACTOR row uses a value set for Department (e.g. {SALES, ENGINEERING}) to express 'regardless of department' — not a dummy placeholder like 'ANY' or 'N/A', and not enumerated as separate rows.
assertions.evidence: CONTRACTOR is enumerated as two separate rows (Contractor Sales and Contractor Engineering), not as a single row with {SALES, ENGINEERING} value set.

assertions.text: The four level×department combinations (SENIOR+SALES, SENIOR+ENGINEERING, JUNIOR+SALES, JUNIOR+ENGINEERING) are all present in the table(s)
assertions.evidence: Senior Sales | SENIOR | SALES, Senior Engineering | SENIOR | ENGINEERING, Junior Sales | JUNIOR | SALES, Junior Engineering | JUNIOR | ENGINEERING

assertions.text: The expected output column contains bonus percentages (e.g. 15%, 12%, 0%) — not bonus amounts. The method returns a percentage, and the table should reflect that.
Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: Method body only contains: Employee employee = new Employee(...); assertEquals(...);

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case (e.g. 'bonusByLevelAndDepartment' → 'Bonus By Level And Department'). Not a generic name like 'test1' or 'testMethod'.
assertions.evidence: Method name 'shouldCalculateBonusPercentage' clearly describes the test intent.

assertions.text: If @Description is present, it provides context beyond what the table rows already express — such as how bonus rates are applied (e.g. as percentage of base salary), or open questions. Does NOT merely restate the column names or summarise what the rows show. It is acceptable to omit @Description if the table already conveys all relevant context.
assertions.evidence: @Description is absent; table conveys all relevant context via column names and rows.

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Only @TableTest is present; no ordering violation.

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
Scenario names describe conditions ('Senior in Sales', 'Contractor regardless of department') — not outcomes ('Gets 15%', 'No bonus').
assertions.evidence: Scenario names: 'Senior Sales', 'Senior Engineering', 'Junior Sales', 'Junior Engineering', 'Contractor Sales', 'Contractor Engineering' all describe conditions, not outcomes.

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Level', 'Department', 'Bonus %') — not implementation terms like 'employeeLevel', 'deptCode', 'result'.
